title.narrative: 2. Score on the Gender Development Index (GDI)

description.narrative: A quantitative external indicator which is a subset of the HDI, the Gender Development Index measures female human development in comparison with male human development in each country. It was added to the UNDP Human Development portfolio in 2014. The GDI computes the difference between male and female scores in the three HDI elements (ability to lead a long and healthy life, measured by life expectancy at birth; the ability to acquire knowledge, measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling; and the ability to achieve a decent standard of living, measured by gross national income per capita). The score assigned effectively illustrates where females are in terms of development in relation to men (where men are set at a score of `1 each year.

title.narrative: 1. Score on the Human Development Index (HDI)

description.narrative: A quantitative external indicator that measures the broad level of human development. Improving the role and contribution of civil society in Nigeria is expected to contribute to increased human development. The Human Development Index (HDI) is about building human capabilities for everyone. The index was created by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 1990 and is updated each year. The HDI is a composite index focusing on three basic dimensions of human development: the ability to lead a long and healthy life, measured by life expectancy at birth; the ability to acquire knowledge, measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling; and the ability to achieve a decent standard of living, measured by gross national income per capita.

title.narrative: 2. Number of CSOs exhibiting evidence of application of ACTsupported CD support (including through PLPs) in at least one of the three focus areas (Internal / Progproj / External)

description.narrative: A quantitative indicator that captures information about CSOs that have changed their behaviour / ways of working following and in line with the capacity development support provided by the ACT programme. Application is where there are specific examples of utilisation of learning from the CD support in the way the CSO functions, according to an independent assessorACTsupported CD is defined as any training, coaching, mentoring or other development support (including involvement in peer learning platforms) that aims to help the CSO manage its processes, stakeholders and/or projects more effectively or efficientlyInternal focus areas are defined as the way CSOs organise themselves and run their internal processes, including governance, strategic planning, human resource management and inhouse operational planning and managementProgrammeProject focus areas are defined as the way CSOs identify, plan, bid for, manage and report on projects or programmes that it delivers in the community or more broadly. External focus areas are defined as the way CSOs behave that impact on their image and influence outside the area of a specific project or programme. Examples include communications and broad stakeholder engagement.
